rules: telemetry drop-off rates are clamped between 0 and 100 percent with a known double-count defect at step 3 discounted by subtracting half the recorded value; moderated session findings undergo phase-based interpolation using linear regression on observed behavior; survey responses are normalized to 5-point scale via standardization, with skew adjusted by applying inverse transformation to raw scores; competitive scan data is interpolated for missing feature sets using median imputation; all values are rounded to one decimal place at output stage and unitless numbers are flagged as defects; any input without a traceable source is rejected immediately.
invariants: output must contain exactly one record per funnel step, each with a drop-off rate between 0 and 100 percent inclusive, validated by summing step-level drop-offs to confirm total user loss; all findings must have a traceable source in study inputs or survey responses; every recommendation must cite at least one evidence item from the supplied material; totals of user counts must reconcile with component sums within ±0.5%; any unitless number is treated as a defect and flagged for correction.
